payload.comment:
Abstention mechanism is arithmetically consistent and functionally correct. Verification: (1) abstain_rate 0.47493 × 7180 = 3410 = human_review_count ✓; (2) selective_risk 0.019629 = 1 − accuracy_on_covered 0.980371 ✓; (3) covered samples = 7180 − 3410 = 3770, errors on covered ≈ 74, errors on abstained ≈ 827, total errors = 901 = 7180 × (1−0.874513) ✓; (4) threshold 0.8499926 calibrated on validation to hit target 0.8 coverage, achieved 0.80008 ✓; (5) predictive_entropy consistently outperforms max_softmax across all three noise severities, as expected ✓; (6) OOD pass with test AUROCs 0.855–0.904 under controlled Gaussian corruption is reasonable ✓.

Primary concern: the validation-to-test coverage gap is 27.5 pp (80.0% → 52.5%). The threshold was set on validation to retain 80% of samples, but on test the model abstains on 47.5%. This is not a bug—the mechanism correctly flags harder test samples (abstained-set accuracy ≈ 75.8% vs covered-set 98.0%)—but it means the operational coverage guarantee derived from validation does not transfer. Downstream consumers expecting ~80% coverage will see only ~52.5% on test. This should be explicitly documented as a distribution-shift effect rather than a calibration failure.

Secondary observations: (a) OOD validation AUROC (0.995) vs test AUROC (~0.89) gap mirrors the coverage gap and reinforces that test is substantially harder; (b) the OOD scope is limited to 'controlled_corruption_proxy' (Gaussian noise only), so real-world OOD robustness is unverified; (c) inherited minor items from prior stages (rotate90 augmentation, patience=3, per-channel normalization qualifier, transformer no-op params in CNN config) remain open documentation gaps but do not affect abstention correctness.

No deterministic findings were raised. The abstention stage is internally consistent and the selective-prediction trade-off is well-characterised. Recommend proceeding with a note that the 52.5% test coverage is the operative figure for deployment planning, not the 80% validation target.
llm_issues: Validation-to-test coverage gap of 27.5 pp (80.0% → 52.5%) means the operational coverage guarantee does not transfer; downstream systems expecting ~80% coverage will see ~52.5% on test
OOD evaluation scope is limited to controlled Gaussian-noise corruption (sigma 0.15/0.25/0.4); real-world OOD robustness (domain shift, novel tissue types, imaging artefacts) is unverified
OOD validation AUROC (0.995) vs test AUROC (~0.89) gap of ~10 pp mirrors the coverage gap and indicates test distribution is substantially harder than validation
Inherited: augmentation 'rotate90' (90° discrete) deviates from research-recommended small-angle jitter; empirically validated but under-documented for reproducibility
Inherited: early_stopping_patience=3 is below the 5–8 range recommended in research notes; low risk given convergence but leaves little margin for slower re-runs
Inherited: normalization labeled 'standardize' without explicit 'per-channel' qualifier; confirm implementation applies per-channel statistics
Inherited: transformer-specific parameters (num_heads, mlp_ratio, pooling, positional_encoding, tokenizer_layers) present in residual_cnn config; likely shared-schema no-ops but unconfirmed
